title: The slot that was booked twice
blurb: Check-then-write holds let two bookings win one slot.
prompt: Two team members booked the same room for the same hour, because the draft read the slot map, checked it in the handler, and wrote the hold in a separate step. The same draft never expired abandoned holds. Review it, fix it, and prove holds are atomic and expiry works.
aiNote: The draft checks slot availability with a read and writes the hold with a later command, so concurrent requests both observe the same free map, and its hold key has no TTL, so an abandoned checkout blocks the slot permanently.
testIdea: Fire two concurrent bookings for one slot and assert exactly one succeeds; abandon a hold and assert it frees after its TTL; reschedule with a replayed key and assert one external calendar event.
followUps: How would you model recurring bookings without a slot explosion?
What should a reschedule do when the new slot is taken?
Which timezone bugs have you seen in booking systems?
